newsitem.title: USA: GM safety expert says Astro recall unlikely.
newsitem.headline: GM safety expert says Astro recall unlikely.

text.p: A leading General Motors Corp (GM) safety expert testified on Thursday it was unlikely GM will recall older Astro minivans to equip them with airbags, despite a $25.4 million verdict for a woman injured while driving an Astro.

Robert Lange, director of safety, told a jury that, since a December verdict against the company GM, engineers have been reviewing safety information about the Chevrolet Astro van, introduced in 1985.

Therese Hunter, 45, received massive brain injuries while driving a 1990 Astro during a collision in northeast Florida six years ago. She now requires full-time assistance and lives in a Miami attended-care facility.
The steering column rammed her jaw and skull and her attorneys argued that General Motors knew such a risk existed before the accident, but did not correct it.

The jurors last December awarded Hunter and her family $25.4 million for her care. That same jury is now weighing punitive damages against GM. Her lawyers on Wednesday asked for $50 million to $75 million in punitive damages.
Lange said he found it "terribly troubling" that the six jurors had reached such a different conclusion than General Motors engineers about the van's safety.
GM engineers are now reviewing safety data about the Astro, Lange said. Introduced in 1985, the Astro sells about 150,000 models each year, attorneys for Hunter said.
Current models of the Astro are equipped with airbags.
The punitive-damages decision could go to the jury as early as Friday.
